The protein encoded by **ARHGAP27** is heavier (~98.4 kDa vs ~83.9 kDa).

<solution>
Comparing the canonical (reviewed, human) UniProt entries:

- **ARHGAP27** (Rho GTPase-activating protein 27, UniProt Q6ZUM4): 889 aa, average mass **98.39 kDa** (UniProt-reported molWeight 98,396 Da — consistent with sequence).
- **MPO** (Myeloperoxidase, UniProt P05164): 745 aa, average mass **83.87 kDa** (computed from sequence; monoisotopic 83.81 kDa).

Therefore the **ARHGAP27**-encoded protein is the heavier one.

{"answer": "ARHGAP27", "concerns": ["The UniProt molWeight field for MPO (P05164) returned an implausible value of 9,000,000,000 Da, which is clearly a data error; the mass was therefore computed directly from the canonical sequence (~83.87 kDa).", "MPO is biologically a glycosylated homodimer (mature enzyme ~150 kDa, functional dimer ~140-150 kDa), so if comparing mature multimeric/glycosylated protein rather than the canonical monomer sequence, MPO would be much heavier; the comparison here uses the canonical UniProt sequence mass for each single chain.", "ARHGAP27 has multiple isoforms; a shorter isoform could be lighter than MPO, so the comparison assumes the canonical (longest, 889 aa) isoform."]}</solution>
